title: Quad unveils security, business, AI plans; Trump offers open line

syllabus: GS2 › Bilateral, regional and global groupings involving India and/or affecting India's interests · GS3 › Security challenges in maritime areas; cyber security; science and technology (AI) · GS4 › Ethics in international relations

answer.t: Started in 2007 and revived in 2017, the Quad met at leaders' level in Manila in November 2026 and announced plans spanning maritime surveillance, AI, cyber security, critical minerals and business.

pts.t: Shared surveillance gives the Indo-Pacific a common picture of what moves at sea, from dark shipping to illegal fishing.
pts.ex: Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration; P-8 and P-3C aircraft in a first Quad exercise in 2027.

pts.t: Regular drills let four navies operate together in anti-submarine and anti-surface warfare.
pts.ex: The 30th Malabar exercise near Japan.

pts.t: The Quad defends open sea lanes and overflight under international law.
pts.ex: Joint statement: 'open, safe and resilient maritime transit corridors'.

pts.t: It rejects unilateral changes to the status quo by force or coercion.
pts.ex: Joint statement on destabilising actions that escalate tensions.

pts.t: The grouping condemns terrorism in all forms, including cross-border terrorism.
pts.ex: A key gain for India given terror from across its western border.

pts.t: Disaster response gives the Quad a non-military face in the region.
pts.ex: Modi lists disaster response among the Quad's core areas.

pts.t: The Quad funds trusted AI access and deployment so the region does not depend on untrusted systems.
pts.ex: Quad AI accelerator to coordinate and fund trusted AI across the Indo-Pacific.

pts.t: Rising cyber incidents need shared standards and response.
pts.ex: Enhanced Quad Cybersecurity Cooperation for 'an open and secure cyberspace'.

pts.t: New deals diversify supply so no member is vulnerable to a single supplier.
pts.ex: Statement's concern over economic coercion through arbitrary export restrictions.

pts.t: Business ties turn diplomatic intent into investment and jobs.
pts.ex: Inaugural Quad Business Leaders' Forum in Mumbai, 2027.

pts.t: Deliverables for smaller states build legitimacy beyond the four members.
pts.ex: Modi: 'trusted solutions for the entire Indo-Pacific'.

pts.t: Supply chains are now treated as a security question.
pts.ex: MEA: cooperation in maritime security, economic security and critical technologies.

pts.t: The Quad is a loose partnership; commitments depend on political will.
pts.ex: Leaders met in Manila for the first time since 2024.

pts.t: Members differ in how far they want to confront China, given deep trade ties.
pts.ex: The Quad meets just before Trump's trilateral with Xi and Putin.

pts.t: India avoids any alliance commitment and keeps ties with Russia.
pts.ex: India's stand of independent foreign policy and multi-alignment.

pts.t: Shifts in US trade and alliance policy can strain partners.
pts.ex: US tariffs on Indian goods in 2025 tested India–US ties.

pts.t: South-East Asian states fear great-power rivalry eclipsing ASEAN centrality.
pts.ex: Modi's own stress on ASEAN unity and centrality at the EAS.

pts.t: Announcements can outrun implementation and funding.
pts.ex: Critics' 'Asian NATO' framing feeds Chinese pushback if delivery lags.

pts.t: Annual leaders' meetings and a light coordination mechanism keep momentum.
pts.ex: A two-year gap before Manila shows the cost of irregular meetings.

pts.t: Prioritise HADR, health, connectivity and training for smaller states.
pts.ex: Quad Vaccine Partnership as an earlier model.

pts.t: Anchor Quad plans in ASEAN-led platforms such as the EAS.
pts.ex: India's Act East Policy and IPOI.

pts.t: Shape norms for trusted, safe and human-centric technology.
pts.ex: India's AI Impact Summit stress on safe, inclusive AI.

pts.t: Joint processing and stockpiling of critical minerals, not just purchase deals.
pts.ex: Quad critical mineral deals announced in Manila.

pts.t: Present the Quad as a provider of public goods, not a military bloc.
pts.ex: Joint statement: 'a force for good and a partnership of action'.

answer.t: From Malabar drills to an AI accelerator and a Mumbai business forum, the Quad is widening its agenda, and its credibility now rests on delivery to the Indo-Pacific.

title: A bullet fired, night call: How 13-member team from India saved a life in Mauritius
where: Front page, continued on page 2 (Divya A)
syllabus: GS2 › India and its neighbourhood (Indian Ocean); India's bilateral relations (Mauritius) · GS4 › Ethics in international relations; compassion
summary: After a young woman was shot near Port Louis amid unrest, Mauritius's Health Minister called India's High Commissioner at night, and a 13-member team from KIMS Hyderabad flew in to operate alongside local doctors; she is recovering.
evolution: Indian Navy rescues the Iranian crew of the Azini, calling India the IOR's 'first responder' (first-responder thread).
ideas: First responder in a crisis: a call from Mauritius's Health Minister to the Indian High Commissioner on the night of October 10 led to a team reaching Mauritius by October 12.
GS2 · India–Mauritius / Indian Ocean
India's overnight medical mission to Mauritius shows the 'first responder' role extending from the sea to hospitals.
Working with, not instead of: doctors judged evacuation to India too risky, so the Indian team operated alongside local doctors; coordination with Mauritian doctors played a major role.
GS2 · Development partnership
Treating the patient in Mauritius with local doctors shows partnership that builds trust and capacity.

Help at a sensitive moment: the shooting, allegedly by a police officer, triggered the most serious unrest in decades; India's help came as the government struggled to restore order and save the patient.
GS2 · Soft power / GS4 · Compassion
Timely humanitarian help during a neighbour's crisis earns goodwill that no treaty can buy.

title: Navy rescues hijacked vessel with Iran crew, IAF lends helping hand

syllabus: GS3 › Security challenges and their management in border areas (maritime security); Various security forces and their mandate · GS2 › India's bilateral relations (Iran); Effect of policies of other countries on India's interests (West Asia) · GS4 › Ethical issues in international relations
summary: The Indian Navy, backed by an IAF C-17 airdrop of Marine Commandos, freed the fishing vessel Azini and its 20 Iranian crew, hijacked by pirates off Somalia last month, in an operation of over 48 hours.
ideas: Piracy as a regional threat: the Navy saw the hijacked vessel as a likely 'mother ship' for launching pirate attacks on merchant shipping, so freeing it protects the sea lanes as well as the crew.
GS3 · Maritime security
Hijacked fishing vessels used as pirate mother ships make piracy a threat to the whole sea lane, not to one crew.
Jointness in action: a mission-deployed warship, a maritime reconnaissance aircraft and Marine Commandos airdropped by an IAF C-17 worked together.
GS3 · Security forces and their mandate
The Azini rescue shows inter-service jointness turning surveillance into swift action at sea.
Restraint as strategy: after persistent surveillance, the Navy used 'calibrated non-kinetic measures' to contain the vessel before its tactical intervention, and all 20 crew were released.
GS3 · Maritime security / GS4 · Proportionality
Calibrated, non-kinetic force secured the hostages' release without escalation: security achieved with restraint.
First responder and preferred security partner: the Navy framed the operation as proof of India's role in the Indian Ocean Region, regardless of the crew's nationality.
GS2 · India and the IOR / GS3 · Security
Rescuing foreign crews builds India's credibility as the Indian Ocean's first responder and preferred security partner.

answer.t: From the Azini rescue to HADR missions, India's Navy is becoming the IOR's first responder; capacity and partnerships will decide how far that role can grow.

title: Why Delhi mustn't take its eyes off Pakistan-Maldives
where: The Ideas Page, page 9 (Aditya Gowdara Shivamurthy, ORF)
syllabus: GS2 › India and its neighbourhood; Bilateral, regional and global groupings · GS3 › Security challenges; Maritime security
summary: Maldives President Muizzu's state visit to Pakistan, with 20 MoUs including defence, shows the Maldives diversifying beyond India; the writer backs India's economic approach but says it must state its security red lines.
ideas: Diversification beyond India: Muizzu's visit produced 20 MoUs, from socio-economic sectors to cybersecurity, drugs and defence and maritime security, and a plan to scale up trade.
GS2 · India–Maldives
Small neighbours are hedging by diversifying partners, testing India's primacy in its neighbourhood.
A crowded defence space: the Maldives also has defence MoUs with China and Turkey, has bought armoured vehicles from the UAE and joined a Saudi-led maritime coalition.
GS2 · Neighbourhood / GS3 · Maritime security
Multiple defence partners for the Maldives crowd the Indian Ocean Region close to India's maritime boundaries.

Pakistan's wider play: since Operation Sindoor, Pakistan and China have held trilaterals with Bangladesh and Afghanistan; Pakistan has pushed SAARC revival, a South Asian bloc without India and a larger naval presence in the Bay of Bengal.
GS2 · Regional groupings
Pakistan is using new regional formats to dilute India's centrality in South Asia.

India's pragmatic economic diplomacy: T-bill extensions, debt restructuring, credit lines and currency swaps build leverage and goodwill without fuelling anti-India nationalism ahead of Maldivian elections.
GS2 · Neighbourhood First / Economic diplomacy
India's economic support builds leverage while avoiding the nationalist backlash that pressure would provoke.
Clear red lines on security: some MoUs (cybercrime, drugs) may even help India, but defence ties with Pakistan need clear communication of India's concerns.
